brief: tilth_search resolves a bare name, `fn name` or `trait Name`, and a Go `func (r *T) Name(...)` signature to definitions (route_query in src/mcp/tools/search_v2.rs). Two other common query shapes miss and cost the agent a retry. (1) A qualified name, `Owner::name` (Rust, C++, PHP) or `Owner.name` (Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, Go), returns no match or falls to a literal text search. (2) A pasted declaration line with a parameter list, for example `pub fn snapshots(&self) -> Guard`, `async fn run(&mut self)`, `def get(self, key):`, `function render(a, b)` or `public void close()`, routes to regex because of its parentheses and returns 0 matches. Add a route before the regex route that recognizes a declaration shape: optional modifier words (pub, pub(crate), async, static, export, public, private, protected, final, abstract, unsafe, const), an optional declaration keyword (fn, def, function, func, class, struct, enum, trait, interface, type), a name that is an identifier or an `Owner::name` or `Owner.name` path of identifiers, and an optional balanced parameter list with an optional return type. Resolve it with route_identifier on the last path segment, and pass the keyword as the kind, as the signature-prefix route does. When a qualifier is present, keep only the definitions whose enclosing owner has that name: a Rust `impl Owner` or `impl Trait for Owner` block (generic parameters removed), a class, struct, interface, enum, trait or module named Owner, or a Go method with that receiver type. is_method_on handles only Go receivers today; generalize it with the outline parent of each definition. When the qualifier keeps no definition, return the definitions of the name without the qualifier and a diagnostic that names the owners found; never return an empty result while the name has definitions. Keep an intentional regex on the regex route: a query that contains a backslash, `[`, `|`, `+`, `?`, `^`, `$` or `.*`, or that does not parse as a declaration shape. Keep dotted text whose last segment has no definition, such as `os.path.join`, on the literal route. Record each rewrite in diagnostics.normalizations, as the Go route does. Add new #[test] fns for each shape, including a qualified query that picks the right one of two same-named methods on different owners.

invariants: a bare-name query returns the same result as before

brief: Search output is the largest remaining cost of the tilth arm. In long sessions, tilth_search returns about 57k characters per session against 46k for a plain grep tool, and about half of it is usage-hit preview text. Each usage hit prints its enclosing construct of up to CONSTRUCT_CONTEXT_MAX_LINES (4) lines (src/search/mod.rs), so a query with many usages prints about four lines per hit. Keep the construct context only where it saves a read: for the first 5 usage hits of a result. Print each later usage hit as one numbered line, `N:content`, as a grep content search does, and record only the printed lines as displayed for the edit gate. Do not change definition output, the file tags in match headers, the JSON fields of the result, or a result with 5 usage hits or fewer. Add new #[test] fns that pin the cutover: a result with more than 5 usage hits prints one line for each later hit, and the lines it records as displayed are exactly the printed lines.

invariants: tilth_read calls per cell do not rise

brief: tilth_write refuses an ast-grep `rewrite` op, and a `replace_text` with all or count, when any matched line was not displayed under the tag. The refusal comes from unseen_message in src/edit/mismatch.rs: `Edit rejected for <path>: line N was never displayed under this tag (displayed: ...)`. For a repeated call-site change, the agent first runs a structural search, whose hits are displayed. A search shows a capped number of hits, so the rewrite of a file with more matches is refused, and the agent spends a read and a retry. Change this case only: the op is a rewrite or an all or count replace_text, the tag matches the live file, and the only reason for the refusal is matched lines that were not displayed. Then the refusal prints the full line span of each such match as `N:content` lines under the `[path#TAG]` header, records exactly those printed lines as displayed for that tag, and says that the same call can now be sent again unchanged. The refused call applies nothing. Keep every other refusal as it is: a drifted tag, a line op, a single-match replace_text, or a file over the tag cap. Add new #[test] fns: a rewrite refused for unseen matches prints them, and the identical second call then applies.

invariants: no edit applies to a line that no response displayed

brief: The edit gate now keeps every line that an earlier read, search, or write result displayed editable, also after a resumed session in a new server process. A replace_text whose `old` matches exactly once in the file needs only the file tag, not displayed lines. Agents still re-read sections before they edit them. In prompts/mcp.md, replace the line that starts `A tilth_write result returns the new tag` with at most two lines that say: lines from any earlier read, search, or write result stay editable, also after a resume, so do not re-read them to edit; for a small change, use replace_text with an exact `old` that occurs once. Keep every other line unchanged, and keep the file under its size cap.

invariants: tilth_write error rate does not rise
